messages:
alex: Heads-up — after the canary we rolled 2026-03-18 21:12 (deploy d3f9), the latency heatmap for /v1/generate shows p95 up ~40ms but p99 looks unchanged. dashboard looks weird, maybe sampling? :thinking:
maria: I saw that too. p50/p95 shifted in the endpoint breakdown but host-level p99 stayed flat. Could be traffic-weighting or the rollup key mismatch.
lee: infra-bot posted the deploy: infra-bot: Deploy d3f9 -> service:api routes: /v1/generate target: canary(10%) :rocket:
az: do we still use route_tag + model_version as the rollup key? if the canary changed model_version tagging then rollups could split.
mar ia: @az (zainab) the canary used model_v2 but the frontend added an extra header X-Route-Variant=canary which our telemetry layer doesn't include in rollups. so split samples might be going to a separate rollup and then aggregated differently. :facepalm:
sam: quick check: are we using tdigest rollups or histogram-approx? If tdigest, heavy tail samples from a small shard can move p95.
lee: we're using tdigest per-route, but we downsample traces for the console (1%) and also have route-weighted rollups for global dashboards. the console p95 uses the rollup that merges by route_name only, not the full variant keys.
az: that mismatch would explain it: canary traffic had a dense block of 500ms+ requests hitting a small bucket; when merged to route_name-only rollup the distribution changed, affecting p95 but not p99 due to interpolation behavior.
alex: is there a query or snippet we can run to prove the split?
lee: run this quick aggregator in metricsql:
```
SELECT tdigest_quantile(rollup_tdigest, 0.95) FROM route_latency WHERE route_name='v1.generate' AND timeframe='5m' GROUP BY route_variant
```

then compare with the merged rollup:
```
SELECT tdigest_quantile(merged_rollup, 0.95) FROM route_latency WHERE route_name='v1.generate' AND timeframe='5m'
```

maria: ran it for 21:10-21:15 — variant=stable p95=120ms, variant=canary p95=210ms, merged p95=160ms. p99 per-variant: stable 400ms, canary 410ms, merged 405ms. so p95 moves more.
sam: that matches a distribution-shape change. tdigest interpolation can under/over-estimate certain quantiles when merging. We've seen p95 change more than p99.
az: UX question — the console shows only the merged number but the rollout page shows per-variant. That mismatch confuses PMs. We should expose both or at least annotate that merged is weight-averaged estimate.
lee: proposal: add a small badge on endpoint charts: "Merged rollup omitted variant headers; see per-variant view" and wire a toggle to show per-variant breakdown. Low-risk UI change.
alex: operational short-term: can we add the X-Route-Variant into the rollup key to avoid split?
maria: we can, but that will explode cardinality — there are ~12 variants across services right now. For this route it might be OK. We should gate by a feature flag and TTL old keys.
sam: long-term: improve merge algorithm — store reservoir samples for tail queries or switch to histogram buckets for p99 stability and tdigest for p50/p95.
az: also update docs and alerting runbooks: our p95 alert fired but p99 didn't — responders assumed no regression. add a note: "quantile sensitivity matters; check per-variant rollups."
lee: I'll open a tiny RFC and a console PR to add the toggle. also file to ops to test the impact of adding X-Route-Variant to rollup key for /v1/generate.
alex: thanks. assigning: lee -> UI, maria -> ops patch for rollup key toggle, sam -> algo follow-up, az -> update runbook.
infra-bot: Created issue INFR-4721: "Per-variant rollup toggle + rollup-key opt-in" (<https://tracker.redwood/INFR-4721>).
alex: great. can we also add a small note in the rollout page that if p95 diverges from p99, check route headers and rollup keys? saves a lot of ping pong. :+1:
lee: will do. quick follow-up: should the console show raw sample counts alongside quantiles? i think that helps interpret noise.
maria: yes, show N and also sampling rate. small change.
az: OK closing — thanks all. :white_check_mark:
